props.gloss_en: one who sees wicked Babylon must bless five blessings
one who saw Babylon says 'Blessed... Who destroyed wicked Babylon'
one who saw Nebuchadnezzar's house says 'Blessed... Who destroyed the house of wicked Nebuchadnezzar'
one who saw the lions' den or the fiery furnace says 'Blessed... Who did miracles for our fathers in this place'
one who saw Mercury says 'Blessed... Who gave patience to those who transgress His will'
one who saw a place from which earth is taken says 'Blessed... Who says and does, decrees and fulfils'
Rava, when he saw donkeys carrying earth, would slap their backs and say: run, righteous ones, to do your Master's will
Mar son of Ravina, when he reached Babylon, would take earth in his kerchief and throw it outside
[he did so] to fulfil what is said: 'and I will sweep it with the broom of destruction' (Isa 14:23)
Rav Ashi: I had not heard Rav Hamnuna's statement, but from my own reasoning I blessed all of them
when Babylon was cursed, its neighbours were cursed
when Samaria was cursed, its neighbours were blessed
as it is written: 'I will make it a possession for the bittern, and pools of water' (Isa 14:23)
as it is written: 'I will make Samaria a heap in the field, a place for planting vineyards' (Mic 1:6)
Rav Hamnuna: one who sees multitudes of Israel says 'Blessed... Who knows secrets'
Rav Hamnuna: one who sees multitudes of gentiles says 'your mother shall be sore ashamed...' (Jer 50:12)
the baraita: one who sees multitudes of Israel says 'Blessed... Who knows secrets'
for their minds are not like one another, and their faces are not like one another
Ben Zoma saw a multitude from a step on the Temple Mount and said 'Blessed... Who knows secrets'
...and 'Blessed... Who created all these to serve me'

how many labours Adam laboured before he found bread to eat (ploughing... baking) and a garment to wear (shearing... weaving), and I rise and find all these prepared before me; all nations hasten to the door of my house, and I rise and find all these before me
what does a good guest say? how much trouble the host took for me -- meat, wine, loaves -- and all his trouble was only for me
but what does a bad guest say? what trouble did this host take? I ate one loaf, one piece, drank one cup; all his trouble was only for his wife and children
of the good guest what does [Scripture] say? 'remember that you magnify his work, of which men have sung' (Job 36:24)
of the bad guest it is written: 'therefore men fear him...' (Job 37:24)
'and the man in the days of Saul was old, come among men' (1 Sam 17:12) -- this is Yishai, David's father
who went out with a multitude, came in with a multitude, and expounded with a multitude
Ulla: we hold [as a tradition]: there is no multitude in Babylonia
it was taught: a multitude is no fewer than six hundred thousand
one who sees the sages of Israel says 'Blessed... Who has apportioned of His wisdom to those who fear Him'
sages of the nations of the world: 'Blessed... Who has given of His wisdom to flesh and blood'
one who sees the kings of Israel says 'Blessed... Who has apportioned of His glory to those who fear Him'
kings of the nations of the world: 'Blessed... Who has given of His glory to flesh and blood'
a person should always strive to run toward the kings of Israel
and not only toward the kings of Israel, but even toward the kings of the nations of the world
so that, if he merits, he will distinguish between the kings of Israel and the kings of the nations
Rav Sheshet was blind; everyone went to greet the king, and Rav Sheshet rose and went with them
the heretic: whole jugs [go] to the river -- where do broken ones [go]?
Rav Sheshet: come see that I know more than you -- at the first and second noisy troops, 'the king is not coming'; at the silence after the third, 'now surely the king is coming'
Rav Sheshet: for earthly kingship is like heavenly kingship

as it is written: 'go out and stand on the mount before the Lord... the Lord was not in the wind... not in the earthquake... not in the fire, and after the fire a still small voice' (1 Kings 19:11-12)
when the king came, Rav Sheshet began to bless him
the heretic: you bless one you do not see?
[the heretic's fate:] his companions put out his eyes
[the heretic's fate:] Rav Sheshet set his eyes on him and he became a heap of bones
R' Sheila had a man flogged who had relations with a gentile woman
asked why he had him flogged, R' Sheila said to them: because he had relations with a female donkey
Elijah came, appearing as a man, and testified
the officials: if so, he is liable to death!
R' Sheila: since the day we were exiled from our land we have no authority to execute; you -- do with him as you wish

R' Sheila recited 'Yours, Lord, is the greatness and the power...' (1 Chr 29:11); asked what he said: 'Blessed is the Merciful One Who gives kingship on earth like the kingship of heaven, and gave you dominion and love of justice'
the officials: the honour of the kingship is so dear to him! -- they gave him a staff and said: judge
the man: does the Merciful One do a miracle for liars like this?
R' Sheila: wicked one, are they not called donkeys?
as it is written: 'whose flesh is the flesh of donkeys' (Ezek 23:20)
seeing him going to tell them that he had called them donkeys, R' Sheila said: this one is a pursuer (rodef) -- and he struck him with the staff and killed him
and the Torah said: if one comes to kill you, rise early to kill him
since a miracle was done for me with this verse, I will expound it: 'Yours, Lord, is the greatness' -- this is the work of creation
and so it says: 'Who does great things past finding out' (Job 9:10)
'and the power' -- this is the Exodus from Egypt
as it is said: 'and Israel saw the great hand...' (Ex 14:31)
'and the glory' -- this is the sun and moon that stood still for Joshua
as it is said: 'and the sun stood still and the moon stayed...' (Josh 10:13)
'and the victory' -- this is the downfall of Rome
and so it says: 'and their lifeblood is sprinkled on My garments...' (Isa 63:3)
'and the majesty' -- this is the war of the streams of Arnon
as it is said: 'therefore it is said in the Book of the Wars of the Lord: Et and Hev in Sufa...' (Num 21:14)
'for all that is in heaven and earth' -- this is the war of Sisera
as it is said: 'from heaven the stars fought, from their courses...' (Judg 5:20)
'Yours, Lord, is the kingdom' -- this is the war of Amalek
and so it says: 'for a hand is upon the throne of the Lord' (Ex 17:16)
'and You are exalted' -- this is the war of Gog and Magog
and so it says: 'behold, I am against you, Gog, chief prince of Meshech and Tubal' (Ezek 38:3)
'as head over all' -- even the overseer of the irrigation well is appointed from Heaven
'Yours, Lord, is the greatness' -- this is the splitting of the Red Sea
'and the power' -- this is the plague of the firstborn
'and the glory' -- this is the giving of the Torah
'and the victory' -- this is Jerusalem
'and the majesty' -- this is the Temple

nodes.label_he: לכל לראש -- אפילו ריש גרגיתא מן שמיא מנו ליה
nodes.label_en: 'as head over all' -- even the overseer of the irrigation well is appointed from Heaven

nodes.label_he: לך ה׳ הגדולה -- זו קריעת ים סוף
nodes.label_en: 'Yours, Lord, is the greatness' -- this is the splitting of the Red Sea

nodes.label_he: והגבורה -- זו מכת בכורות
nodes.label_en: 'and the power' -- this is the plague of the firstborn

nodes.label_he: והתפארת -- זו מתן תורה
nodes.label_en: 'and the glory' -- this is the giving of the Torah

nodes.label_he: והנצח -- זו ירושלים
nodes.label_en: 'and the victory' -- this is Jerusalem

nodes.label_he: וההוד -- זו בית המקדש
nodes.label_en: 'and the majesty' -- this is the Temple
